thread:
jess: hey folks — first-week setup question. I'm running docker-compose up for the local stack and the postgres container is exiting immediately. Logs show initdb permission errors. mounting ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data in compose on mac, any ideas?

jess: logs: ```postgres_1  | initdb: could not change permissions of directory \"/var/lib/postgresql/data\": Permission denied
postgres_1  | initdb: removing contents of data directory \"/var/lib/postgresql/data\"
postgres_1  | Database system is shut down```

ryan: hey jess — welcome! this is almost always a bind-mount ownership issue. postgres in the official image runs as UID 999, so if the host dir is owned by your user the container can't change perms. two easy approaches: 
- chown the host dir to 999:999
- or use a Docker named volume instead of a host bind mount (recommended for local dev unless you need host files)

ryan: quick commands: 
```bash
sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata
# or from a container if sudo chown fails:
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data
```

ryan: minimal compose snippet using a named volume (no host mount): ```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
volumes:
  pgdata: {}
```

ryan: also make sure you're using a multi-arch postgres image (postgres:15 is fine) on Apple Silicon — but that won't affect perms.

jess: tried sudo chown -R 999:999 and still getting \"Operation not permitted\" when chown runs. i'm on mac with my home dir encrypted, maybe that's it.

infra-bot: FYI if the repo dir is on iCloud/SMB/NFS or an encrypted volume, macOS can block chown. In that case named volume is the path of least resistance.

ryan: yep — if chown is blocked, create a named volume OR set up the data dir inside the container and copy data in via init scripts. If you need to seed data or see files on host, you can also run the chown from an ephemeral container (the alpine example above often works even when host chown fails).

jess: ran the alpine chown command and that fixed it — postgres started up. thanks!

onboarding-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @jess! If you hit more local infra stuff check https://internal.docs/redwood/local-dev-db and DM #devex. :tada:
